nodes.html: Business Growth Adviser — what we can help with
nodes.text: Business Growth Adviser — what we can help with

nodes.html: A growth adviser is the accountant who asks 'how can we improve the business?' rather than 'have you got your receipts?'. They model pricing scenarios, identify margin leaks, forecast cash flow under growth stress, and help you decide whether to hire, acquire, or hold. This is the difference between a compliance accountant and a growth partner — and the right one depends on where your business is.

nodes.html: A growth adviser gives you board-level financial oversight without a full-time salary. Typical services include monthly management reporting, cash-flow forecasting, budgeting vs actuals analysis, KPI dashboards, board-pack preparation, and strategic decision support. Our matched growth advisers offer advisory packages tailored to your scale — whether you are a $1m or $20m business.

nodes.html: Pricing, margin analysis & M&A due diligence
nodes.text: Pricing, margin analysis & M&A due diligence

nodes.html: Margin analysis draws on cost-volume-profit (CVP) analysis and pricing strategy — core management accounting competencies that identify where margin leaks and help you set prices with confidence. For acquisitions, mid-market accounting practices regularly perform buy-side financial due diligence on a project-fee basis, including Quality of Earnings analysis, balance sheet reviews, and working capital checks. There is an important regulatory boundary to understand: providing financial due diligence or general valuation work on a business target does not require an Australian Financial Services Licence (AFSL). However, where an acquisition involves structuring regulated financial products, advice must be delivered by an appropriately licensed entity under the Corporations Act 2001 (Cth). Our matched growth advisers are clear about where their expertise ends and where licensed financial advice is required.

nodes.q: How is a growth adviser different from my accountant?
nodes.a: A compliance accountant looks backward (filing last year's return); a growth adviser looks forward (improving this year's performance). Many firms offer both, and some businesses use the same firm for compliance and advisory. In the questionnaire, tell us whether you want forward-looking growth advice specifically and we will match accordingly.
